findings.reason: The approved QC13 design has no ε < 1/2 restriction on the Rz problem, but this Definition narrows it. Preserve ε ≥ 1/2 cases with the zero-T Clifford construction in lem-qc-rz-determinant-one-reduction, and align alg-qc-rz-clifford-t-approximation, thm-qc-rz-approximation-correct-on-termination, and thm-qc-rz-clifford-t-tcount; recheck consumers after any Definition change.

The optional Q(k) factoring branch permits suggested factor lists but specifies no factor-suggestion procedure, call interface, or exact budget handling. Define that bounded procedure as an input or remove the branch; check alg-qc-rz-clifford-t-approximation and its correctness and T-count consumers.

Step 3 can return TIMEOUT when a finite total candidate budget is exhausted, but that budget is absent from the Inputs. Declare the budget and its exhaustion rule; recheck thm-qc-rz-approximation-correct-on-termination and thm-qc-rz-clifford-t-tcount.

Steps 1.2–1.3 use integer Bézout to exclude a conjugation-fixed prime class and to show odd integers are not divisible by δ, but neither derive nor declare thm-bezout-identity. This can be repaired locally with the explicit odd-p identity 2((p+1)/2) - p = 1 and an explicit odd-factor argument.

Step 1.2 calls diag(λ,1) and λ⁻¹I lattice maps when constructing the shifted map, but step 1.1 only verifies R, A, B, K, X, Z, and L. Verify these additional maps and their inverses on the lattice generators.

Step 2.3 infers infinitely many solvable classes from F7, which proves a first-success tail bound rather than the tail after every finite index. From A1 and the candidate exponent growth bound, show the tail sum of prime-indicator probabilities diverges, so the tail failure products vanish and m'' exists.
Verification 1.2 identifies the top-left entry of Rz(π/16) as e^(iπ/32); the stated Rz convention gives e^(-iπ/32). Use the lower-right entry for ζ64 or use ζ64⁻¹ in the field-degree argument.
